name: ENPRO

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter is that my DCF is the wrong instrument, not that my growth number is too low. A two-stage FCFF model with a 2% terminal growth rate and a 10.8% WACC systematically undervalues a business whose value is in a long compounding runway — it forces almost all of the value into an explicit five-year window and then caps the rest at inflation. The market is not underwriting 31% FCFF growth for five years; it is underwriting a durable 10-12% compounder that deserves a 20x terminal EBITDA multiple, and those are very different statements that this model cannot distinguish. And the bull evidence is partly VISIBLE, not hypothetical: AST grew 21.8% organically last quarter, margins expanded 90bp, and guidance was raised.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Four to six quarters of AST organic growth sustained above 20% with total adjusted EBITDA margin above 27%, and Sealing organic growth holding at 5%+ through a soft industrial tape. That would establish the mix shift as durable rather than cyclical.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, in part — and this is the strongest evidence against my own verdict. Q2 AST organic growth of 21.8%, margin +90bp, guidance raised twice. I take it seriously.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I cannot resolve whether the correct terminal multiple for EnPro is an industrial one or a semiconductor one, and that single choice moves the fair value more than any growth assumption I could make. What I CAN say is that the gap does not close under the bull case within this model's frame: at 15% growth the fair value is $151, at 20% it is $188, and only at 31.3% does it reach $295. Even granting AST 20% growth for five years and Sealing 4%, blended FCFF growth lands well short of 31%. So the price requires either a growth rate I cannot construct from the segment arithmetic, or a terminal multiple this model does not offer. I record rich on that basis, with the terminal-multiple objection unresolved and stated.

what_changed: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-04 (8-K item 2.02, EX-99.1). Sales $338.8M, +17.6% total and +10.9% organic. Adjusted EBITDA $86.9M versus $71.1M, margin 25.6% versus 24.7%. Advanced Surface Technologies sales +21.8% ORGANIC on leading-edge precision cleaning and semiconductor capital equipment. Sealing Technologies sales +15.3%, or +5.0% excluding FX and the AlpHa Measurement Solutions and Overlook Industries acquisitions completed in Q4 2025 — so most of Sealing's headline growth was bought. H1 free cash flow $61.4M on $90.9M of operating cash flow after $29.5M of capex, versus $52.8M and $73.2M last year. Full-year 2026 guidance RAISED to revenue growth of 14-16%, adjusted EBITDA $330-340M, adjusted EPS $9.30-9.80. No company-specific news in the store for 90 days; the sector feed carries a soft August ISM print and 'why industrial stocks could keep losing steam', which is consistent with the stock's -10.0% 21-day move.
consensus_case: EnPro has stopped being an industrial conglomerate and is being repriced as a semiconductor and advanced-materials compounder. Advanced Surface Technologies grew sales 21.8% organically in Q2 on leading-edge precision cleaning and semiconductor capital equipment demand; total sales rose 17.6% to $338.8M; adjusted EBITDA rose 22.2% to $86.9M at a 25.6% margin (+90bp); and management RAISED full-year 2026 guidance to 14-16% revenue growth, $330-340M of adjusted EBITDA and $9.30-9.80 of adjusted EPS. Sealing Technologies underneath it is a genuinely high-quality aftermarket business with pricing power and low cyclicality. The market pays 20x forward EBITDA because it is underwriting AST becoming the majority of the earnings mix at semiconductor-equipment growth rates and semiconductor-equipment multiples, with Sealing's cash flow funding it. That is a coherent thesis, and the Q2 print is evidence for it, not against it.
base_case_rationale: I underwrite 9% five-year FCFF growth. The mix argument is real: if AST is roughly 40% of EBITDA growing at 15-20% and Sealing is 60% growing at 4-5% organically, blended EBITDA growth is 9-11% before any margin expansion, and EnPro converts EBITDA to free cash flow at a reasonable rate (H1: $61.4M of FCF against $163.3M of adjusted EBITDA, seasonally understated). I decline to extrapolate the headline 14-16% because guidance itself discloses that a large part of it is the AlpHa and Overlook acquisitions annualising, and organic Sealing growth is 5.0%. I also note the five-year revenue CAGR is 1.3% — this company has not compounded before, and the semiconductor cycle it is now levered to is the most violent capex cycle in industrials. 9% is my estimate of what a good outcome looks like without assuming the up-cycle never ends.
key_risks: Semiconductor capital-equipment cycle: AST is levered to fab tool builds, not installed base
A large share of headline 2026 growth is the AlpHa and Overlook acquisitions annualising, not organic
Five-year revenue CAGR is 1.3% — the compounding record is short
At 20x forward EBITDA against an Industrials cohort median of 14.3x, multiple compression is the dominant risk to the equity, not earnings
Legacy asbestos and environmental liabilities in the sealing business
watch_for: AST organic growth falling below the high teens in any quarter — the first sign the mix thesis is cyclical
Full-year adjusted EBITDA landing outside the raised $330-340M range
Any further acquisition that inflates headline growth while diluting organic disclosure
